rounds.text: The company's profitability and capital efficiency are exceptional, evidenced by a 5-year compounded profit growth rate of 23% [E19] and a 10-year median return on equity of 21% [E25]. Fundamental strength is further underscored by aggressive debt reduction, with borrowings dropping sharply from Rs 14.04 Cr to Rs 4.00 Cr in Mar 2026, leading to a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.12x [E37, E38]. Furthermore, cash generation is pristine, with operating cash flow reaching Rs 12.67 Cr in Mar 2026—representing a stellar cash conversion rate of 2.23x against reported profit [E33, E34]. Insider conviction is visibly strengthening, as promoters have increased their holding by 3.45 percentage points to 74.98% by Jun 2026 [E40]. Conceded: [E24], compounded share price growth over 1 year is -2%.

Conceded: [E19] and [E25], the 5-year profit growth and 10-year median ROE are indeed high. However, the bull's reliance on backward-looking profit and return metrics masks severe momentum fatigue and structural volatility, as evidenced by a 1-year share price return of -2% [E24] and an annualized volatility sitting at an extreme 310.6% [E51]. While debt reduction to Rs 4.00 Cr and a 0.12x debt-to-equity ratio are highlighted [E37, E38], the engine flags a critical warning that earnings growth is actively decelerating [E63]. Furthermore, the quarterly operating-margin trend is classified as inconsistent over the last three quarters [E32], and the worst peak-to-trough drawdown on record reaches a catastrophic -83.8% [E50]. Finally, while promoter buying is cited [E40], institutional money flow remains strictly neutral [E41], suggesting that sophisticated market participants refuse to chase the bull's narrative despite the historical cash generation [E34].
